To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression levels of the genes involved in the early development of GTs are affected by estrogen exposure.
the expression of some key genes in the development of the male genital tubercle is altered by estrogen exposure.
the expressions of shh and Fgf-8 genes were decreased by estrogen in male genital tubercle, and that the expressions of eph-b2 and fg-10 genes were not affected by estrogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of genital malformation in humans, especially Hypospadiac conditions.
the molecular mechanisms of the development of external genitalia, and it may be useful in the understanding of the pathophysiology of Hypospadiac cases.
the molecular mechanisms of GT development and the effects of endocrine disrupting agents on these mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of shh and/or fgf-8 can be considered as the most reliable markers for the early phase, while efn-b2, eph-b2 and fg-f10 can be considered as markers for the late phase of GT morphogenesis.
the expression patterns of these genes are different in males and females, but their expressions are more sensitive to estrogenic exposure in males than in females.
the early phase of the morphogenesis of GT is mainly regulated by shh and fg-8, while the late phase of development is mainly regulated by efn-b2, eph-b2 and fg-10.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

shh and fg-8 are critical genes for GT development, but their expressions can be affected by estrogenic compounds, and thus, they can be used as markers for the detection of endocrine disrupters in future.
shh and fg-8 are the main genes that can be affected by estrogens in GT development, but efn-b2 is the most resistant gene to estrogen exposure in the GT development.
the early stage GT development is mainly regulated by the mesenchyme, while the urethral epithelium is the major regulator of the later stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genes that are expressed during the early phases of the GT development are more sensitive to estrogenic effects.
the genes that play critical roles in the morphogenesis of the genital organs can be affected by estrogenic exposure in utero.
the sex specific expression of the genes in the genital tubercle is not a simple matter.
